_comment: OPS-CLAIM-VERIFIER-COVERAGE-W1 — the host-path claims made by the prescriptive docs (vault CLAUDE.md), routed to the daily reconciler so each is checked LOCALLY on the host that owns it. CI never gets SSH; the verifier asserts COVERAGE (every host-path claim has a row here or an exemption with a reason), the reconciler asserts TRUTH on-host. Two projections of one fact, never two probes that can disagree.
_why_not_ssh_from_ci: monitoring-inventory-reconcile.py already runs daily on each host (signal-1 57 6, aoe-1 17 7) with per-host row ownership via MONITORING_HOST_LABELS. On those hosts these paths are LOCAL FILES — no SSH required at all. Building a second reporter, or giving CI prod credentials, would both be strictly worse.
_why_inventory_membership_is_not_coverag: MEASURED 2026-08-02, not reasoned: simulating a DELETED /opt/algovault-monitoring/send_telegram.sh against the live inventory fires NOTHING. HASH_DRIFT skips a file it cannot find (by design — 'absence is DARK/ORPHAN's business'), DARK only evaluates rows carrying a `schedule` and the wrapper's is null, and ORPHAN runs host→repo so a missing file is invisible to it. The shared alert wrapper that CLAUDE.md forbids consumers from re-implementing could therefore vanish from a host in silence. DOC_PATH_CLAIM closes exactly that hole, which is why rows here are kept for artifacts that ALSO have an inventory row — it is not duplication, it is the one assertion the inventory delegates away.

_expect_semantics.present: the path MUST exist on every owning host. Absent ⇒ MISSING finding.
_expect_semantics.absent: an INVERSE claim — the doc prescribes this path as a FUTURE target and it must NOT exist yet. Present ⇒ REVIEW finding (the doc's 'do this later' has silently become 'someone did it').

_unreachable_is_not_a_pass: A claim whose owning host is not THIS instance is reported DEFERRED, never silently skipped — the verdict-token principle at per-check granularity. A skipped claim must never read identically to a passing one.

claims.source: CLAUDE.md — Operator-action-required alert contract; the shared wrapper consumers MUST NOT re-implement
claims.reason: Load-bearing on BOTH hosts and the one primitive whose second installation went unrecorded for 7 days (OPS-AOE-MONITORING-PARITY-W1). Its existence is restated in prose because a mid-incident reader needs the path; the row is what keeps that restatement honest.
Named in CLAUDE.md as the daily congruency canary; a TG-alert responder is sent to this exact path. signal-1 only — measured ABSENT on aoe-1 2026-08-02, which is correct, not drift.
The autopilot entry point cited by the alert contract; postgres runs only on signal-1.

INVERSE claim. This is a FUTURE extraction target, not an installed artifact — the 3-example-threshold rule names it as what to build at the 3rd consumer. Measured ABSENT on both hosts 2026-08-02. If it ever appears, the extraction happened and CLAUDE.md's 'until' clause is stale — which is a doc correction, not an ops fault.

claims.source: CLAUDE.md — Deploy pipeline; holds .venv beside the source, so a deploy swaps per manifest entry
claims.reason: The whole-directory-swap hazard is argued FROM this path's layout; if the path moved, that law's reasoning would silently stop applying to the real deploy root.

The interpreter the systemd units actually exec. This is the single path whose disappearance the 'never whole-directory-swap' law exists to prevent, so it is the highest-value existence check of the set.
Canonical deploy dir named by the deploy law; also the server.json path the registry-conformance canary validates. Trailing slash normalised away — the claim is about the directory.

exempt_claims.reason: PROSE ELLIPSIS, not a path — CLAUDE.md's 'structurally dark once installed to /opt/... while every gate stays green'. Three ASCII dots, so the template detector's Unicode-ellipsis rule does not catch it. Probing it would fire forever.
A docker MOUNT SPEC (note the :ro suffix), not a filesystem path. The claim is about the mount being cosmetic (socket access is root-equivalent), not about a file existing.

A measurement CITATION from the ugrep forensics ('/usr/bin/grep → 73'), naming the system binary used as a control. Present on every Linux/macOS box by definition; checking it asserts nothing about AlgoVault.

CONTAINER-scoped path, deliberately asserted ABSENT at runtime by CLAUDE.md itself (a Stage-1 build input whose content reaches prod via dist/knowledge/*.json). Not a host path; the reconciler runs on the host, not inside the app container.
CONTAINER-scoped deployed-artifact path used to teach the tsc-emits-per-module lesson. Same reason as /app/audits/ — the host filesystem is the wrong place to look for it.
CONTAINER-scoped, and the literal at the centre of the wave that shipped an unsatisfiable AC. Kept in the doc precisely as the counter-example; probing it on a host would fire forever.
